title: Micro pilot outreach fieldnotes: Noviwell (rapid experiment)
content:
Quick top-line: lightweight, testable outbound to Noviwell (mid-market digital health platform). Goal: validate messaging that ties Redwood Dedicated benefits to their stated priorities (data isolation + latency for triage workflows). Success criteria for pilot: 5 qualified discovery calls from 80 targeted contacts within 6 weeks OR a reply rate >= 6% and demo conversion >= 15% among replies.

Why Noviwell?
- Product: clinician-facing triage & intake; sensitive PII, needs low-latency suggestions for care routing.
- Tech signals: AWS-hosted + uses Intercom for patient messaging (public engineering job postings mention AWS/Golang).
- Buying triggers: security/compliance, latency SLAs for triage path, desire to reduce operational overhead of self-hosting models.

Experiment design (N=80, 4x cohorts of 20):
- Cohort A (control): generic outbound (value = accuracy + lower TCO).
- Cohort B (latency-first): emphasize sub-100ms inference, routing/fallbacks, Dedicated.
- Cohort C (compliance-first): focus on Private/VPC, KMS/HSM, audit trails.
- Cohort D (platform dev experience): SDKs, rollouts, tracing + Console.

Cadence (per contact):
- Day 0: short cold email (A/B subject lines), LinkedIn connection + 1-line DM if connection succeeds.
- Day 3: follow-up email with one-pager (attach lightweight one-pager PDF link).
- Day 7: value-add note (mini case study: how X reduced per-token latency and cut cost via batching).
- Day 14: last touch ask for a 15 min intro + optional calendar link.

Metrics to track (sheet):
- opens, replies, meetings booked, demo->POC interest, reasons for pass, feedback tags (security, price, timing, unknown).
- We'll track by cohort and by persona (CTO/Head of ML/VP Product).

Sample subjects (test these):
- "Can Noviwell avoid triage delays without a rewrite?"
- "Reduce triage latency + keep PHI in your VPC"
- "15 min: latency & compliance pattern for clinical triage models"

Cold email (short pattern — 3 lines + CTA):
Hi [First],

Saw Noviwell is expanding clinician triage flows — quick question: are you currently running the LLM parts in a VPC or on a hosted endpoint?

We help teams keep PHI inside their cloud while getting sub-100ms inference for patient triage (Dedicated pools + KV prefix caching). Would you be open to a 15-min chat to see if this would drop latency and ops overhead for Noviwell?

If yes, here’s my calendar: [cal link] — if not, who’s a better contact?

Phone / 30s cold call script:
- Intro: "Asha from Redwood Inference — quick check: are you the person who owns model serving for triage?"
- If yes, pitch in 2 sentences: "We run a dedicated inference runtime that lets teams put models in their VPC or on-hosted Dedicated nodes; customers see consistent sub-100ms p95 and fewer bursts of throttling.
- Close ask: "15 minutes to see if this maps to what you're solving?"

Objection handling cheatsheet:
- "We can’t put PHI outside our environment": "Totally — we support Private deployments with customer-managed control plane + KMS/HSM integrations; many health customers treated model inference as in-scope for data residency."
- "We host our own models already": "Understood — teams often still outsource inference to Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and less ops. We can run a short POC focused on a critical path (e.g., triage scoring) so you can compare unit economics and latency without migrating everything."
- "Price concerns": "We suggest a narrow POC window and instrument token-level costs + latency in Console; typical outcome is neutral-to-positive on cost after batching/caching + improved latency SLOs. We can cap spending in the POC."
- "We already use X vendor": "Great — curious whether their latency/cost tradeoffs meet production SLAs. We can run a 1-week head-to-head on a synthetic traffic profile if that's valuable."

Research notes (contacts & personas):
- Primary target: Head of ML / ML Platform. Secondary: CTO, VP of Eng (platform).
- Names to approach (LinkedIn scrapes): Priya Ram (Head of ML), Marcus Boyd (CTO), Julianne Kerr (Dir Eng).
- Best inbound signals: job posting for "ML infra" or "MLOps engineer", public uptime incidents mentioning latency, new product launches that add real-time features.

One-pager bullets (for attach):
- What: Dedicated + Private inference with Dev-first API + Console for observability.
- Why: sub-100ms p95 for short sequences; autoscaling + predictable pricing; VPC/private control plane.
- Proof points: ded. customer X (anom name) improved triage p95 from 320ms -> 95ms and reduced ops tickets by 60% (anecdotal).

POC ask (if they bite):
- 2-week POC scope: integrate one triage model (3-5M params or similar) behind Redwood Dedicated or Private, run synthetic traffic for 72h, compare p95, p99, cost/token, and production tracing.
- Deliverables: dashboard link, summary memo, next-step recommendation.

Risks / unknowns to capture during discovery:
- model size they plan to serve (Llama variants vs smaller fine-tuned), sequence length distribution, peak QPS, compliance constraints (HIPAA/SOC2).
- internal procurement cadence & procurement contacts.

Notes to self / next micro tasks (this week):
- Finalize email variants and load into Outreach sequence (Asha).
- Create one-pager PDF and upload to S3 + public link (Carlos).
- Seed first 20 contacts (Lena) and log initial opens/replies to the experiment sheet (link in linked_artifacts).
- Prep a 1-week synthetic-test harness note for Eng infra team to be ready if a POC is agreed.

Freeform scribbles / raw ideas:
- Try a subject line referencing a timing metric ("Cut triage wait by 60% — 15 min chat?").
- Consider offering a "latency snapshot": 1-page comparison based on public endpoints + a short script they can run locally to capture p95 baseline (makes the convo concrete).
- If Priya is unresponsive, call Marcus with the "ops tickets" angle (reduced on-call/ops work).

End of notes. Keep this doc light — iterate after first 20 replies.
